en.name: Parsley, fresh
en.summary: Fresh parsley keeps 2–3 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 3–4 months in the freezer. The fridge figure is short for such a sturdy-looking herb, which makes freezing a surplus bunch genuinely worthwhile.
en.pantry: No room-temperature timeline is published for fresh parsley. It is a high-moisture leaf on a soft stem and it wilts noticeably within hours in a warm kitchen. Standing the trimmed stems in a glass of water will keep a bunch presentable while you cook, but it is not a storage method here — get it into the fridge, or chop and freeze what you will not use.
en.fridge: 2–3 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. That is a tight window, so handle the bunch well: do not wash it until you use it, wrap it loosely in dry kitchen paper inside a bag or box, and keep it in the crisper where the humidity is steadier. Parsley yellows from the outside of the bunch inwards, so pull the outer sprigs first and strip off any yellow leaves before they spread. A bunch stood in water with a loose bag over the top also works well.
en.freezer: 3–4 months in the freezer, and this is the answer to the short fridge window. Wash and dry the parsley thoroughly, strip the leaves, chop them and freeze them flat in a bag, or pack them into an ice-cube tray with a little water or oil. Frozen parsley is limp and will not garnish anything, but it goes straight into a soup, a sauce, a stuffing or a tabbouleh dressing with the flavour intact. The stems are worth freezing separately for stock.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Add frozen chopped parsley straight to the dish; thawed parsley collapses into a wet clump.
spoilage: Yellowing leaves, usually starting at the outside of the bunch.
Blackened, slimy leaves or slime at the cut ends.
A sour or musty smell instead of a clean, green one.
Mould on the stems in a closed bag.
tips: Do not wash it until you use it; wet parsley rots within a day.
Freeze chopped leaves flat in a bag so you can break off what you need.
Save the stems for stock — they carry as much flavour as the leaves.
Buy a bunch only when you have a use for most of it, and freeze the rest the same day.

faq.q: How long does fresh parsley keep?
faq.a: 2–3 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 3–4 months in the freezer.
Yes, 3–4 months. Chop and freeze it flat in a bag or in oil cubes. It will not work as a garnish afterwards, but the flavour survives for cooking.

faq.q: How do you keep parsley fresh longer?
faq.a: Keep it dry and cold: unwashed, loosely wrapped in dry kitchen paper in the crisper, or stems in water with a loose bag over the top.

zh.name: 新鮮巴西里
zh.summary: 新鮮巴西里放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 2～3 天，冷凍則是 3～4 個月。對一種看起來這麼結實的香草來說，冷藏的數字相當短——這也讓「把多的那一把冷凍起來」變成真正划算的事。
zh.pantry: 新鮮巴西里沒有公布的室溫期限。它是長在軟莖上的高含水量葉片，在溫暖的廚房裡幾個小時就明顯萎軟。把剪過的莖插進水杯，可以讓它在你做菜的時候維持體面，但那在這裡不算保存方法——請放進冰箱，或把用不到的部分切碎冷凍。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 2～3 天。窗口很緊，所以處理要講究：要用時才洗，用乾的廚房紙巾鬆鬆包好、裝進袋子或盒子，放濕度比較穩定的蔬果室。巴西里是從整束外圍往內發黃的，所以先用外圈的枝條，並且在黃葉擴散前把它摘掉。把整束插進水裡、上面鬆罩一個袋子，效果也很好。
zh.freezer: 冷凍 3～4 個月——這就是對付冷藏短窗口的答案。請把巴西里徹底洗淨擦乾，摘下葉子切碎，平鋪裝袋冷凍；或填進製冰盒、加一點水或油。冷凍過的巴西里軟塌，擺盤是沒指望了，但直接丟進湯、醬汁、填餡或塔布勒沙拉醬裡，風味完好。莖另外冷凍起來煮高湯也很值得。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。冷凍碎巴西里直接加進菜裡；解凍後會塌成一團濕泥。
spoilage: 葉子發黃，通常從整束外圍開始。
葉子發黑黏滑，或切口出現黏液。
聞起來酸或有霉味，而不是乾淨的青草味。
tips: 要用時才洗；濕的巴西里一天就爛。
切碎後平鋪裝袋冷凍，要用時剝一塊就好。
莖留下來煮高湯——它的香氣不輸葉子。
確定大部分用得掉才買一把，剩下的當天就冷凍。

faq.q: 新鮮巴西里可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 天，或冷凍 3～4 個月。
可以，3～4 個月。切碎平鋪裝袋，或做成油冰塊。之後不能擺盤，但入菜的風味完好。

faq.q: 怎麼讓巴西里放久一點？
faq.a: 保持乾燥與低溫：不要洗，用乾廚房紙巾鬆鬆包好放蔬果室；或莖插水、上面鬆罩袋子。
